rubrics.provenance: Automatically tokenized supplied proposed facet criteria; nine pilot decompositions drafted for this experiment; no independent teacher approval. Three pilot rubrics revised using AI development feedback; no independent human approval.

concepts.name: Historical sources and their two main classes

points.text: Sources provide evidence of past human activity.
Literary sources include books and written documents.
Archaeological sources include physical remains such as coins buildings and inscriptions.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Explain that sources give evidence about past human activity, and distinguish literary books/documents from archaeological physical remains with a meaningful example or description of each.

concepts.name: Local literary sources: Deepawamsa and Mahawamsa

points.text: Deepawamsa is the earlier chronicle dating to the fourth century AD.
Mahanama wrote Mahawamsa and later writers continued the account.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Identify Deepawamsa as the earlier chronicle (about 4th century AD) and explain Mahawamsa, including Mahanama and its later/continuous historical account. Do not require memorizing every minor title.

concepts.name: Foreign literary sources and authors

points.text: Foreign writers recorded Sri Lankan history including Fa Hsien and Robert Knox.
Distinguish visitors from writers relying on information supplied by others.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Explain that foreigners wrote about Sri Lanka, give at least one accurate writer/text example and distinguish writers who visited from those who relied on other people’s information.

concepts.name: Critically checking historical accounts

points.text: Check who wrote a source when why and how it was produced.
Compare accounts with other sources including inscriptions to corroborate events.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Consider when/who/why/how a source was produced, and use other sources such as inscriptions to corroborate events rather than treating one written account as certain.

concepts.name: Epigraphy and inscriptions

points.text: Epigraphy is writing on stone or other materials including cave pillar copper plate inscriptions.
Inscriptions record historical events and social facts.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Recognize writing on stone or other materials; identify at least two inscription forms or media; explain at least one type of historical event or social fact inscriptions record.

concepts.name: Ancient coins as historical evidence

points.text: Ancient coins include Kahapana and Thamba Massa.
Coins reveal commerce metal use and trade.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Correctly identify at least two coin types or provenances mentioned in the book, and explain what coins reveal about commerce, metal use, or trade.

concepts.name: Ruins, art, and antiquities

points.text: Physical remains include ruins drawings sculptures and antiquities.
Remains reveal architecture water management clothing and beliefs.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Discuss at least two of ruins, drawings/sculptures and antiquities, including meaningful information they reveal (such as architecture, water management, clothing or beliefs).

concepts.name: Benefits of studying history

points.text: History develops critical logical thinking and learning from past experience.
History helps social identity respect and tolerance.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Explain at least two distinct benefits in substance, including either critical/logical understanding from past experience or social identity/respect/tolerance.

concepts.name: Threats to and protection of archaeological sources

points.text: Vandalism and urbanization can destroy monuments and archaeological remains.
Citizens should protect archaeological remains to preserve historical evidence.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Describe at least one concrete cause of destruction and at least one protective behaviour or civic responsibility, linking protection to preserving historical evidence.

concepts.name: Prehistoric human settlement

points.text: The text places early human habitation in Sri Lanka at about 125,000 years ago and discusses Homo sapiens.
Early inhabitants survived through hunting and gathering while adapting to different environments.

concepts.sourceCriteria: The text places early human habitation in Sri Lanka at about 125,000 years ago and discusses Homo sapiens. Early inhabitants survived through hunting and gathering while adapting to different environments.

concepts.name: Prehistoric archaeological evidence

points.text: Rathnapura gem-mine gravel deposits preserve old stone tools and animal remains.
The Iranamadu Formation and prehistoric cave sites are also used to investigate early settlements.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Rathnapura gem-mine gravel deposits preserve old stone tools and animal remains. The Iranamadu Formation and prehistoric cave sites are also used to investigate early settlements.

concepts.name: Prehistoric ways of life

points.text: Prehistoric groups used stone tools and collected food from their surroundings.
Their lifestyles and material culture varied as they adjusted to rainfall and regional conditions.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Prehistoric groups used stone tools and collected food from their surroundings. Their lifestyles and material culture varied as they adjusted to rainfall and regional conditions.

concepts.name: Protohistoric settlements and burial

points.text: The protohistoric period included changes toward agriculture and more settled communities.
Megalithic burial grounds offer evidence of beliefs and practices associated with the dead.

concepts.sourceCriteria: The protohistoric period included changes toward agriculture and more settled communities. Megalithic burial grounds offer evidence of beliefs and practices associated with the dead.

concepts.name: Early historical villages and towns

points.text: In early historical times, the village household head was known as a Gahapathi.
Intermediate settlements called Nagara linked village products and larger trading cities.

concepts.sourceCriteria: In early historical times, the village household head was known as a Gahapathi. Intermediate settlements called Nagara linked village products and larger trading cities.

concepts.name: Leadership in the pre-state era

points.text: Before island-wide kingship, prosperous regional chieftains held power over local areas.
Early inscriptions use the title Parumaka for such leaders.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Before island-wide kingship, prosperous regional chieftains held power over local areas. Early inscriptions use the title Parumaka for such leaders.

concepts.name: Village organization and authority

points.text: A Gamika served as a village leader in early society.
Village leadership was linked to wider networks of regional chieftains and local households.

concepts.sourceCriteria: A Gamika served as a village leader in early society. Village leadership was linked to wider networks of regional chieftains and local households.

concepts.name: Growth of central political power

points.text: Control of multiple regions developed from dispersed chiefdoms toward centralized political rule.
Trade and the need to organize regional authority helped encourage political integration.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Control of multiple regions developed from dispersed chiefdoms toward centralized political rule. Trade and the need to organize regional authority helped encourage political integration.

concepts.name: Nature of the early state

points.text: The lesson distinguishes pre-state local authority from a state exercising wider, more organized power.
The emergence of kingship involved governing institutions, resources and authority over a larger territory.

concepts.sourceCriteria: The lesson distinguishes pre-state local authority from a state exercising wider, more organized power. The emergence of kingship involved governing institutions, resources and authority over a larger territory.

concepts.name: Ancient kings and reunification

points.text: King Dutugemunu is associated with unifying power across regions in the ancient period.
King Vijayabahu I later opposed Chola power and worked to re-establish independent kingship.

concepts.sourceCriteria: King Dutugemunu is associated with unifying power across regions in the ancient period. King Vijayabahu I later opposed Chola power and worked to re-establish independent kingship.

concepts.name: Ancient rulers and administration

points.text: Kings relied on officers and other local leaders to carry out administration.
The population included ordinary villagers whose activities formed much of social history.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Kings relied on officers and other local leaders to carry out administration. The population included ordinary villagers whose activities formed much of social history.

concepts.name: Farming and irrigation economy

points.text: Agriculture was central to the economy of ancient Sri Lankan settlements.
Tanks and irrigation arrangements supported crop production in areas with seasonal rainfall.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Agriculture was central to the economy of ancient Sri Lankan settlements. Tanks and irrigation arrangements supported crop production in areas with seasonal rainfall.

concepts.name: Trade and merchants

points.text: Internal and overseas exchange formed part of the island’s ancient economy.
Foreign merchant groups and trade routes connected Sri Lanka with other regions.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Internal and overseas exchange formed part of the island’s ancient economy. Foreign merchant groups and trade routes connected Sri Lanka with other regions.

concepts.name: Occupations and livelihoods

points.text: Ordinary people worked in crafts, farming and other occupations that sustained communities.
Evidence about the general public complements chronicles that focus on rulers and elites.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Ordinary people worked in crafts, farming and other occupations that sustained communities. Evidence about the general public complements chronicles that focus on rulers and elites.

concepts.name: Religion and cultural coexistence

points.text: Religious institutions influenced ancient social and cultural life.
The text records interactions and coexistence among Buddhists, Hindus, Muslims and other groups.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Religious institutions influenced ancient social and cultural life. The text records interactions and coexistence among Buddhists, Hindus, Muslims and other groups.

concepts.name: Scientific observation in ancient life

points.text: Ancient communities learned from nature and used practical observations in everyday activities.
Their accumulated experience shaped engineering and other technical achievements.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Ancient communities learned from nature and used practical observations in everyday activities. Their accumulated experience shaped engineering and other technical achievements.

concepts.name: Ancient irrigation technology

points.text: Building and maintaining reservoirs demanded understanding of water movement and land conditions.
Sri Lankan irrigation works show applied knowledge rather than random construction.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Building and maintaining reservoirs demanded understanding of water movement and land conditions. Sri Lankan irrigation works show applied knowledge rather than random construction.

concepts.name: Construction and architecture

points.text: Ancient builders made foundations and structures using carefully arranged materials.
The construction of stupas illustrates planned work and practical understanding of stability.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Ancient builders made foundations and structures using carefully arranged materials. The construction of stupas illustrates planned work and practical understanding of stability.

concepts.name: Ancient roads and bridges

points.text: Roads linked major settlements and important routes in ancient Sri Lanka.
Stone bridges were constructed to cross rivers, including approaches near Anuradhapura.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Roads linked major settlements and important routes in ancient Sri Lanka. Stone bridges were constructed to cross rivers, including approaches near Anuradhapura.

concepts.name: Traditional time measurement

points.text: Ancient terminology distinguished months and time divisions in practical use.
Terms such as Vasa or Havajara referred to a year and Thithiya to a day.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Ancient terminology distinguished months and time divisions in practical use. Terms such as Vasa or Havajara referred to a year and Thithiya to a day.

concepts.name: Social organization and hierarchy

points.text: Ancient social organization arranged roles in hierarchies linking kings, officials and communities.
The lesson distinguishes vertical hierarchies from groups of people with similar rank or authority.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Ancient social organization arranged roles in hierarchies linking kings, officials and communities. The lesson distinguishes vertical hierarchies from groups of people with similar rank or authority.

concepts.name: Law and customary traditions

points.text: Written rules and accepted traditions helped organize conduct in society.
Law and tradition were used to address antisocial behaviour and maintain social cohesion.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Written rules and accepted traditions helped organize conduct in society. Law and tradition were used to address antisocial behaviour and maintain social cohesion.

concepts.name: Ancient taxes and administration

points.text: Ancient revenue included taxes linked to agriculture and the use of water.
The Dakapathi tax concerned tank water, while other taxes were collected for cultivating royal land or catching fish.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Ancient revenue included taxes linked to agriculture and the use of water. The Dakapathi tax concerned tank water, while other taxes were collected for cultivating royal land or catching fish.

concepts.name: Ancient money and exchange

points.text: Ancient communities used ways of exchanging goods and assessing payments.
Trade and financial practices are evidence of organized economic relationships.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Ancient communities used ways of exchanging goods and assessing payments. Trade and financial practices are evidence of organized economic relationships.

concepts.name: Environmental and cultural knowledge

points.text: Historical practices include attention to local food and the natural environment.
Understanding these practices can inform present-day sustainability and protection of heritage.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Historical practices include attention to local food and the natural environment. Understanding these practices can inform present-day sustainability and protection of heritage.

concepts.name: First urbanization and ancient cities

points.text: Anuradhapura and Polonnaruwa were major centres of ancient urban life.
The growth of cities depended on administration, economic surplus and exchanges.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Anuradhapura and Polonnaruwa were major centres of ancient urban life. The growth of cities depended on administration, economic surplus and exchanges.

concepts.name: Downfall of Polonnaruwa

points.text: Struggles for the throne after powerful rulers weakened the Polonnaruwa kingdom.
Economic difficulties and external pressures also contributed to its decline.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Struggles for the throne after powerful rulers weakened the Polonnaruwa kingdom. Economic difficulties and external pressures also contributed to its decline.

concepts.name: Shift toward southwest kingdoms

points.text: After dry-zone urban centres weakened, political centres moved to new locations.
Dambadeniya and Yapahuwa became important in the changing pattern of kingship.

concepts.sourceCriteria: After dry-zone urban centres weakened, political centres moved to new locations. Dambadeniya and Yapahuwa became important in the changing pattern of kingship.

concepts.name: Defence and changing capitals

points.text: Rulers had to protect their capitals against rebellion and foreign attacks.
Buvanekabahu I selected Yapahuwa as a safer royal centre after difficulties at Dambadeniya.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Rulers had to protect their capitals against rebellion and foreign attacks. Buvanekabahu I selected Yapahuwa as a safer royal centre after difficulties at Dambadeniya.

concepts.name: Second urbanization

points.text: The lesson distinguishes the second phase of urban growth from the earlier dry-zone city pattern.
Changing political centres and commerce shaped new towns and kingdoms in the southwest.

concepts.sourceCriteria: The lesson distinguishes the second phase of urban growth from the earlier dry-zone city pattern. Changing political centres and commerce shaped new towns and kingdoms in the southwest.

concepts.name: Historical role of the Kandyan kingdom

points.text: The Kandyan kingdom continued as an independent inland kingdom after other kingdoms declined.
Its rulers resisted several outside pressures before British annexation in 1815.

concepts.sourceCriteria: The Kandyan kingdom continued as an independent inland kingdom after other kingdoms declined. Its rulers resisted several outside pressures before British annexation in 1815.

concepts.name: Vimaladharmasuriya I and legitimacy

points.text: Vimaladharmasuriya I strengthened his position by marrying Kusumasana Devi.
He also embraced Buddhism and brought the Sacred Tooth Relic to Kandy.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Vimaladharmasuriya I strengthened his position by marrying Kusumasana Devi. He also embraced Buddhism and brought the Sacred Tooth Relic to Kandy.

concepts.name: Kandyan dynasties and succession

points.text: Royal succession changed with marriages and dynastic relationships.
After Narendrasinghe died without an heir, rulers of the Nayakkar dynasty came to power.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Royal succession changed with marriages and dynastic relationships. After Narendrasinghe died without an heir, rulers of the Nayakkar dynasty came to power.

concepts.name: Kandyan administration and justice

points.text: The Kandyan kingdom had ranked officials and a governing structure centred on the king.
The king personally heard important disputes including treason and temple-related cases.

concepts.sourceCriteria: The Kandyan kingdom had ranked officials and a governing structure centred on the king. The king personally heard important disputes including treason and temple-related cases.

concepts.name: Kandyan agricultural economy

points.text: Agriculture was the main basis of Kandyan economic life.
Production was largely directed toward local consumption and the needs of the kingdom.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Agriculture was the main basis of Kandyan economic life. Production was largely directed toward local consumption and the needs of the kingdom.

concepts.name: Meaning and origins of Renaissance

points.text: The Renaissance was a European revival in art and learning between the fourteenth and sixteenth centuries.
The revival began in Italian centres including Florence and drew interest toward classical learning.

concepts.sourceCriteria: The Renaissance was a European revival in art and learning between the fourteenth and sixteenth centuries. The revival began in Italian centres including Florence and drew interest toward classical learning.

concepts.name: Humanism and new thought

points.text: Renaissance scholarship renewed interest in Greek and Roman texts and human activities.
This outlook encouraged investigation, creativity and changes in established thinking.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Renaissance scholarship renewed interest in Greek and Roman texts and human activities. This outlook encouraged investigation, creativity and changes in established thinking.

concepts.name: Art and literature during Renaissance

points.text: Painting, sculpture, architecture and literature developed with renewed attention to technique.
These changes formed part of the broader cultural and academic revival in Europe.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Painting, sculpture, architecture and literature developed with renewed attention to technique. These changes formed part of the broader cultural and academic revival in Europe.

concepts.name: Science and printing

points.text: Scientific observation and new inventions became features of the Renaissance.
Gutenberg’s printing machine supported wider circulation of knowledge and books.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Scientific observation and new inventions became features of the Renaissance. Gutenberg’s printing machine supported wider circulation of knowledge and books.

concepts.name: Exploration and effects on Sri Lanka

points.text: European search for trade routes expanded contacts with Asian regions.
These changes in trade and navigation eventually affected relations between Europeans and Sri Lanka.

concepts.sourceCriteria: European search for trade routes expanded contacts with Asian regions. These changes in trade and navigation eventually affected relations between Europeans and Sri Lanka.

concepts.name: Portuguese maritime expansion

points.text: The Portuguese sought access to Asian trade and valuable eastern commodities.
They also attempted to spread Christianity along with commercial influence.

concepts.sourceCriteria: The Portuguese sought access to Asian trade and valuable eastern commodities. They also attempted to spread Christianity along with commercial influence.

concepts.name: Sri Lanka when Portuguese arrived

points.text: Several political centres existed in Sri Lanka at the time of Portuguese arrival.
Kotte and other kingdoms responded differently to Portuguese commercial and military ambitions.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Several political centres existed in Sri Lanka at the time of Portuguese arrival. Kotte and other kingdoms responded differently to Portuguese commercial and military ambitions.

concepts.name: Struggles with Seethawaka

points.text: The Seethawaka kingdom fought Portuguese expansion over a prolonged period.
Its lack of sufficient naval strength limited efforts against coastal Portuguese power.

concepts.sourceCriteria: The Seethawaka kingdom fought Portuguese expansion over a prolonged period. Its lack of sufficient naval strength limited efforts against coastal Portuguese power.

concepts.name: Portuguese religious and political role

points.text: Portuguese influence extended from coastal trade into political and religious activity.
Their involvement produced alliances and conflicts with local rulers.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Portuguese influence extended from coastal trade into political and religious activity. Their involvement produced alliances and conflicts with local rulers.

concepts.name: Dutch power in Sri Lanka

points.text: The Dutch replaced Portuguese rule in much of the island’s coastal region.
Dutch fortresses and commercial interests shaped the later coastal political situation.

concepts.sourceCriteria: The Dutch replaced Portuguese rule in much of the island’s coastal region. Dutch fortresses and commercial interests shaped the later coastal political situation.

concepts.name: Origins of the Industrial Revolution

points.text: Industrial Revolution began in Britain in the later eighteenth century with greater machine production.
Capital, colonial markets, resources and political conditions helped Britain industrialize first.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Industrial Revolution began in Britain in the later eighteenth century with greater machine production. Capital, colonial markets, resources and political conditions helped Britain industrialize first.

concepts.name: Textile machinery development

points.text: James Hargreaves produced the Spinning Jenny to improve spinning.
Richard Arkwright developed water-powered spinning and Crompton produced the Mule.

concepts.sourceCriteria: James Hargreaves produced the Spinning Jenny to improve spinning. Richard Arkwright developed water-powered spinning and Crompton produced the Mule.

concepts.name: Iron steel and coal industries

points.text: Demand for machinery encouraged new iron and steel production methods.
Coal supplied fuel while mining and steam machinery were improved to support industrial growth.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Demand for machinery encouraged new iron and steel production methods. Coal supplied fuel while mining and steam machinery were improved to support industrial growth.

concepts.name: Transport innovations

points.text: Macadam developed a new method of road construction to improve travel.
Steam locomotives and steam-powered ships expanded the movement of people and goods.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Macadam developed a new method of road construction to improve travel. Steam locomotives and steam-powered ships expanded the movement of people and goods.

concepts.name: Communication and social changes

points.text: Industrial growth increased the need for faster, cheaper communication and postal services.
It also changed employment, urban populations and living conditions.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Industrial growth increased the need for faster, cheaper communication and postal services. It also changed employment, urban populations and living conditions.

concepts.name: British strategic interests in Sri Lanka

points.text: Britain valued Sri Lanka for its position on Indian Ocean sea routes.
Trincomalee harbour was important for naval security around India.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Britain valued the island’s position on Indian Ocean sea routes. Trincomalee harbour was strategically important for naval security, especially around India.

concepts.name: British takeover of Dutch possessions

points.text: European conflict contributed to British moves against Dutch-held coastal territories.
The Kew letter was connected to the British campaign, and Trincomalee was attacked in 1795.

concepts.sourceCriteria: European conflict contributed to British moves against Dutch-held coastal territories. The Kew letter was connected to the British campaign, and Trincomalee was attacked in 1795.

concepts.name: British political ambitions in Kandy

points.text: After occupying coastal areas, the British sought influence over the Kandyan kingdom.
Disputes and rivalries around succession also affected relations between Kandyan leaders and the British.

concepts.sourceCriteria: After occupying coastal areas, the British sought influence over the Kandyan kingdom. Disputes and rivalries around succession also affected relations between Kandyan leaders and the British.

concepts.name: Kandyan Convention and annexation

points.text: The Kandyan kingdom came under British rule in 1815.
This ended the independent Kandyan monarchy and expanded British control over the whole island.

concepts.sourceCriteria: The Kandyan kingdom came under British rule in 1815. This ended the independent Kandyan monarchy and expanded British control over the whole island.

concepts.name: Rebellions against British rule

points.text: Resistance arose against British authority, including the 1818 and 1848 uprisings.
British military strength, roads and organization affected the outcomes of these struggles.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Resistance arose against British authority, including the 1818 and 1848 uprisings. British military strength, roads and organization affected the outcomes of these struggles.

concepts.name: National and religious renaissance

points.text: The lesson identifies a period of religious and national revival from about 1850 to 1915.
Political agitation gained greater prominence in the later struggle for independence.

concepts.sourceCriteria: The lesson identifies a period of religious and national revival from about 1850 to 1915. Political agitation gained greater prominence in the later struggle for independence.

concepts.name: Christian missionary activity

points.text: Missionary groups used preaching and schools to spread Christianity under British rule.
English education was linked to employment opportunities in colonial administration.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Missionary groups used preaching and schools to spread Christianity under British rule. English education was linked to employment opportunities in colonial administration.

concepts.name: Buddhist revival and schooling

points.text: Buddhist leaders and supporters organized religious and educational revival activities.
They helped establish Buddhist schools such as Ananda and Dharmaraja.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Buddhist leaders and supporters organized religious and educational revival activities. They helped establish Buddhist schools such as Ananda and Dharmaraja.

concepts.name: Hindu revival and education

points.text: Arumuga Navalar promoted Hindu religious education and Tamil cultural learning.
Hindu schools and organizations were established as part of the revival.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Arumuga Navalar promoted Hindu religious education and Tamil cultural learning. Hindu schools and organizations were established as part of the revival.

concepts.name: Muslim educational revival

points.text: Siddhi Lebbe encouraged Muslim education and knowledge of English and Arabic.
T. B. Jayah later helped expand Muslim schooling and educational leadership.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Siddhi Lebbe encouraged Muslim education and knowledge of English and Arabic. T. B. Jayah later helped expand Muslim schooling and educational leadership.

concepts.name: Colebrooke-Cameron reforms

points.text: The reforms of 1833 reorganized British colonial government and administration.
Councils were established and administrative divisions reshaped.

concepts.sourceCriteria: The reforms of 1833 reorganized British colonial government and administration. They established councils and reshaped the island’s administrative divisions.

concepts.name: Crew-McCallum reforms

points.text: The Crew-McCallum changes provided limited electoral representation.
The Legislative Council was enlarged while most people still had no vote.

concepts.sourceCriteria: The Crew-McCallum changes provided limited electoral representation. The Legislative Council was enlarged while most people still had no vote.

concepts.name: Manning constitutional reforms

points.text: Manning reforms increased the representation of unofficial members in the Legislative Council.
Their elections remained based on restricted franchise rather than universal voting.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Manning reforms increased the representation of unofficial members in the Legislative Council. Their elections remained based on restricted franchise rather than universal voting.

concepts.name: Donoughmore constitution

points.text: The Donoughmore reforms introduced universal adult franchise in 1931.
The State Council formed an important stage in constitutional development.

concepts.sourceCriteria: The Donoughmore reforms introduced universal adult franchise in 1931. The State Council formed an important stage in constitutional development.

concepts.name: Soulbury constitutional reforms

points.text: The Soulbury proposals prepared a parliamentary form of government.
They were important to the constitutional changes surrounding independence in 1948.

concepts.sourceCriteria: The Soulbury proposals prepared a parliamentary form of government. They were important to the constitutional changes surrounding independence in 1948.

concepts.name: Plantation economy under Britain

points.text: British economic policies encouraged export-oriented plantation agriculture.
Coffee, tea and rubber growing transformed economic activity and land use.

concepts.sourceCriteria: British economic policies encouraged export-oriented plantation agriculture. Coffee, tea and rubber growing transformed economic activity and land use.

concepts.name: Transport and infrastructure changes

points.text: Colonial export industries prompted construction of roads and railways.
These routes connected plantation areas to ports and commercial centres.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Colonial export industries prompted construction of roads and railways. These routes connected plantation areas to ports and commercial centres.

concepts.name: Economic and social inequalities

points.text: Plantation development changed employment patterns and local communities.
Urban labourers often had low pay, uncertain hours and few protections.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Plantation development changed employment patterns and local communities. Urban labourers often had low pay, uncertain hours and few protections.

concepts.name: Workers and trade unions

points.text: Workers formed unions and organized protests to improve conditions.
Examples of early urban labour action included strikes by printers and other workers.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Workers formed unions and organized protests to improve conditions. Examples of early urban labour action included strikes by printers and other workers.

concepts.name: Cultural and educational changes

points.text: British rule altered institutions and access to English-language education.
These changes contributed to new professions and groups in society.

concepts.sourceCriteria: British rule altered institutions and access to English-language education. These changes contributed to new professions and groups in society.

concepts.name: Soulbury reform and independence

points.text: The Soulbury Commission proposed constitutional changes in the 1940s.
Sri Lanka achieved independence in 1948 with a parliamentary form of government.

concepts.sourceCriteria: The Soulbury Commission proposed constitutional changes in the 1940s. Sri Lanka achieved independence in 1948 with a parliamentary form of government.

concepts.name: Features of the 1972 constitution

points.text: The constitution adopted in 1972 changed the political framework of independent Sri Lanka.
It established the country as a republic instead of retaining the earlier Dominion arrangement.

concepts.sourceCriteria: The constitution adopted in 1972 changed the political framework of independent Sri Lanka. It established the country as a republic instead of retaining the earlier Dominion arrangement.

concepts.name: Features of the 1978 constitution

points.text: The 1978 constitution introduced a system based on an executive presidency.
It also provided a more extensive chapter on fundamental rights than the 1972 constitution.

concepts.sourceCriteria: The 1978 constitution introduced a system based on an executive presidency. It also provided a more extensive chapter on fundamental rights than the 1972 constitution.

concepts.name: Economic development after independence

points.text: Post-independence policy included changes in agriculture, industry and economic planning.
Governments took different steps to develop livelihoods and national production.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Post-independence policy included changes in agriculture, industry and economic planning. Governments took different steps to develop livelihoods and national production.

concepts.name: Social welfare and political participation

points.text: Universal franchise increased attention to ordinary people’s needs in government policy.
Education and other social welfare measures expanded as responses to social inequality.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Universal franchise increased attention to ordinary people’s needs in government policy. Education and other social welfare measures expanded as responses to social inequality.

concepts.name: Meaning and examples of political revolutions

points.text: A political revolution brings major changes to governing power in a relatively short time.
American, French and Russian revolutions are studied as examples of that change.

concepts.sourceCriteria: A political revolution brings major changes to governing power in a relatively short time. American, French and Russian revolutions are studied as examples of that change.

concepts.name: American struggle for independence

points.text: North American colonies challenged British political control and taxation.
Their struggle led to independence and a new political system.

concepts.sourceCriteria: North American colonies challenged British political control and taxation. Their struggle led to independence and a new political system.

concepts.name: French Revolution causes

points.text: Economic and social inequalities under the old French monarchy increased discontent.
Royal privilege and political separation from ordinary people helped fuel the French Revolution.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Economic and social inequalities under the old French monarchy increased discontent. Royal privilege and political separation from ordinary people helped fuel the French Revolution.

concepts.name: French Revolution outcomes

points.text: Revolution in France weakened absolute monarchy and challenged inherited privilege.
Ideas concerning liberty and equality gained greater political significance.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Revolution in France weakened absolute monarchy and challenged inherited privilege. Ideas concerning liberty and equality gained greater political significance.

concepts.name: Russian Revolution of 1917

points.text: Russian political and social tensions contributed to the revolutionary movements of 1917.
The Bolshevik leadership under Lenin captured major institutions in the October Revolution.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Russian political and social tensions contributed to the revolutionary movements of 1917. The Bolshevik leadership under Lenin captured major institutions in the October Revolution.

concepts.name: Causes of World War I

points.text: Rivalries and alliances among European powers helped produce World War I.
The war began in Europe and spread through the participation of several major powers.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Rivalries and alliances among European powers helped produce World War I. The war began in Europe and spread through the participation of several major powers.

concepts.name: Results of World War I

points.text: The First World War caused extensive deaths, destruction and political change.
International attempts to prevent another war included the League of Nations.

concepts.sourceCriteria: The First World War caused extensive deaths, destruction and political change. International attempts to prevent another war included the League of Nations.

concepts.name: Causes of World War II

points.text: Aggressive policies of Germany, Italy and Japan increased international tensions.
The League of Nations was unable to prevent the escalation toward another world war.

concepts.sourceCriteria: Aggressive policies of Germany, Italy and Japan increased international tensions. The League of Nations was unable to prevent the escalation toward another world war.

concepts.name: Consequences of World War II

points.text: The Second World War had disastrous effects on people and states across continents.
The desire to prevent further wars encouraged stronger international cooperation.

concepts.sourceCriteria: The Second World War had disastrous effects on people and states across continents. The desire to prevent further wars encouraged stronger international cooperation.

concepts.name: United Nations and its functions

points.text: The United Nations was created to promote international peace and cooperation.
Its bodies include the General Assembly, Security Council and Secretariat.

concepts.sourceCriteria: The United Nations was created to promote international peace and cooperation. Its bodies include the General Assembly, Security Council and Secretariat.
